display.purpose: Page titles — the single h1 per view.

title.purpose: Card and section headings; hierarchy by weight, not size.

body.purpose: Default text size for the whole interface, including controls.

label.purpose: Metadata, counts, section eyebrows, breadcrumbs, status pills.

small.purpose: Chips, counts, and secondary metadata below body size.

micro.purpose: Tiny inline affordances and caret hints.

nano.purpose: Smallest uppercase badges and matched-field markers.

body-sm.purpose: Embed note bodies and dense secondary text.

stat.purpose: Dashboard figure value — the large number over a quiet label.

prose-h1.purpose: Document title in the reading/article view.

cloud.purpose: Data-driven tag chip size; the only type that scales with frequency, not role.

mono.purpose: Code, file paths, and machine identifiers shown literally.

shadows.name: search-results
shadows.purpose: Graph/search result list floating over content.

shadows.name: palette
shadows.purpose: Command palette — the deepest floating layer.

shadows.name: floating-lg
shadows.purpose: Block toolbar and larger raised surfaces.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition for background and border-color on controls.

motion.name: ease-press
motion.purpose: Fast press feedback (translateY) on active controls.

motion.name: ease-panel
motion.purpose: Transform easing for panels and sliding surfaces.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single do-the-thing action per view region (approve, save, create).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font: inherit; background: var(--accent); color: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--accent); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); padding: 6px 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease, border-color 0.15s ease, transform 0.05s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-primary:active { filter: brightness(0.95); transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Default control — everything that is not the one primary action.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { font: inherit; color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--btn-border); background: var(--btn-bg); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); padding: 6px 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease, border-color 0.15s ease, transform 0.05s ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--bg-alt); border-color: var(--accent); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The raised content surface; flat at rest, bounded by a 1px hairline.
components.html:
Recently modified

Notes the agent touched most recently.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--bg-card); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius); padding: 16px; color: var(--text); } .ds-card h2 { margin: 0 0 10px; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-card p { margin: 0; color: var(--text-dim); font-size: 13px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Field and search input; focus is a 2px accent outline, never a glow.
components.css: .ds-input { font: inherit; background: var(--bg-card); color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); padding: 8px 10px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--text-dim); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 1px; border-color: var(--accent); }

components.name: Nav Item
components.description: Sidebar navigation row; recedes when inactive, uses the soft accent when current.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; } .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: var(--radius-sm); color: var(--text-dim); text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; font-size: 15px; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--bg-alt); color: var(--text); } .ds-nav-item-active { background: var(--accent-soft); color: var(--accent); }

components.name: Tag Chip
components.description: Discrete token for tags and statuses; the only pill-radius element.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; background: var(--accent-soft); color: var(--accent); border-radius: var(--radius-pill); padding: 1px 8px; font-size: 12px; }

components.name: Stat
components.description: Signature at-a-glance figure: a large number over a quiet label.
components.css: .ds-stat { background: var(--bg-card); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius); padding: 16px; } .ds-stat-value { font-size: 24px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--text); } .ds-stat-label { color: var(--text-dim); font-size: 13px; }

narrative.overview:
Doug KX is a working instrument, not a showcase. It is a knowledge-operating surface laid over a real Obsidian vault: an agent proposes and a human approves, and the interface exists to make that loop fast, legible, and trustworthy. The visual world is dark-first — a near-black canvas with a single blue signal accent — because the tool is used for long, focused sessions where the content, not the chrome, must hold attention.

The voice is authoritative: precise, quiet, and unhedged. The interface states what is true (what changed, what is orphaned, what is pending approval) without decoration or apology. Every affordance earns its place; nothing is ornamental. Density is high but never crowded, because structure — hairlines, tonal layering, and a strict accent budget — carries the hierarchy that ornament would otherwise be asked to do.

Components feel refined and restrained: quiet controls that recede so the content is the interface. Depth is deliberately shallow — surfaces are flat at rest and separated by 1px low-contrast hairlines and tonal steps, not by heavy shadows. Shadow is reserved for genuinely floating layers (menus, the command palette, popovers) so that "raised" always means "temporarily above the document." The result reads as a precision tool: calm, ordered, and dependable under the hand.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, near-black canvas with one blue signal accent.
Authoritative, low-noise voice: state facts, skip decoration.
Refined and restrained controls that recede behind the content.
Flat by default; hairlines and tone create structure, shadows only for floating layers.
One accent used sparingly — its rarity is what makes it a signal.
Native system type; no webfonts, no waiting, no drift.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: The accent appears on ≤10% of any given screen. Its scarcity is the point — if everything is blue, nothing is.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px hairlines and tonal steps, never with heavy strokes or fills. If a region needs to separate from its neighbor, change its tone or add a hairline — do not reach for a shadow.

rules.name: The Native Type Rule
rules.body: No webfonts. The system UI font is the interface; adding a display face would add latency and break the tool's native immediacy.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Section headings stay at 15px and separate themselves by weight (600) and color, not by growing. Only the page title earns a larger size.

rules.name: The Scroll-Once Rule
rules.body: The page frame never scrolls; exactly one region inside it does. Navigation and identity stay put while content moves.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow appears only when an element leaves the document flow — never to decorate a card that is simply sitting in the page.

rules.name: The Pill-Is-A-Token Rule
rules.body: Fully round shapes are reserved for discrete tokens — tags and statuses. Buttons, cards, and inputs never use the pill radius; their soft-cornered rectangle is what says "control" or "container."

dos: Do keep the accent to ≤10% of a screen — buttons, links, active nav, and selection only (The One Signal Rule).
Do build structure from 1px hairlines and tonal steps (canvas → panel → card) before reaching for any other separator (The Hairline Rule).
Do reserve shadows for genuinely floating layers; a card at rest is flat (The Flat-By-Default Rule).
Do use the system UI font and let weight (600) carry section hierarchy instead of size (The Native Type Rule, The Weight-Not-Size Rule).
Do match radius to role: 6px controls, 10px cards, 14px large panels, 999px chips.
Do use the semantic hues only for state (success / warning / danger) — never as decorative color.
donts: Don't introduce a webfont, a display face, or any typeface beyond the system UI and mono stacks.
Don't use the pill radius on buttons, cards, or inputs — round means "token," not "control."
Don't add a shadow to an element that is not floating above the document.
Don't use the accent as a fill for large surfaces or as decoration; it marks interaction and current state only.
Don't replace hairline separation with heavy strokes, thick borders, or filled dividers.
Don't invent additional accent hues — one signal color, plus the three semantic states.
